subject: Science
title: Year 9 Science Exam 2
topic: Inheritance & chemical reactions · AQA Higher · Paper A
intro: Calculator allowed. Relative atomic masses (A<sub>r</sub>): C = 12, O = 16, Ca = 40, Cu = 64. For longer answers write in full sentences and use key words. Describe = say what happens; Explain = say what happens and why (use because and so); Compare = similarities and differences (use whereas); Evaluate = points for and against, then a justified conclusion. 6-mark questions are marked on how well your ideas link together: plan for a minute, then write about 6 linked points.

questions.q:
Polydactyly is an inherited condition in which a person has extra fingers or toes. It is caused by a dominant allele, D.
Which term describes a genotype with two identical alleles, such as dd?
questions.ms: homozygous (1).

questions.q:
A father with polydactyly has the genotype Dd. The mother does not have polydactyly.
Write out a genetic diagram to show the possible genotypes of their children: give the mother's genotype, both parents' gametes and the four offspring genotypes.
questions.ms: Mother's genotype dd (1); gametes D and d from the father, d and d from the mother (1); offspring Dd, Dd, dd, dd (1).

questions.q: Give the probability that their child will have polydactyly, as a percentage. (%)
Explain why a person with polydactyly could have either the genotype DD or the genotype Dd.
questions.ms: D is dominant, so only one copy is needed for it to be expressed (1); so DD and Dd both give the polydactyly phenotype (1).

questions.q: Height in humans shows continuous variation. Explain why height varies so much between people.
questions.ms: Any three: controlled by many genes (1); also affected by the environment (1), e.g. diet / nutrition (1); gives a range of values rather than separate groups (1).

questions.q:
Peppered moths rest on tree trunks during the day, where birds hunt them. The moths are either pale or dark.
• Before the 1800s, most tree trunks in England were pale, and most peppered moths were pale.
• During the Industrial Revolution, soot from factories made tree trunks black.
• By 1895, about 98% of peppered moths near cities were dark.
Explain how natural selection caused the dark form of the peppered moth to become more common.
questions.ms: Level-marked. Level 3 (5–6): detailed and coherent, points linked in a logical sequence, correct terms. Level 2 (3–4): several relevant points with some linking. Level 1 (1–2): simple, separate statements. 0: nothing relevant. Indicative: variation in colour caused by mutation / different alleles; soot made trunks dark; pale moths no longer camouflaged so eaten by birds; dark moths camouflaged, less likely eaten; dark moths survived and reproduced; passed on the dark allele; over many generations the dark allele became more common. Level 3 links camouflage to survival AND to passing on alleles over generations.

questions.q: A horse and a donkey can mate. Their offspring is called a mule. Mules are infertile. Explain why horses and donkeys are classified as different species.
questions.ms: Members of the same species breed to produce fertile offspring (1); mules are infertile, so horses and donkeys are different species (1).

questions.q: Explain how the introduction of a new predator into a habitat could cause a species to become extinct.
questions.ms: Prey has no adaptations to escape the new predator (1); it eats so many that the population falls until none survive (1). Allow: outcompetes another species for food.

questions.q:
A student investigates how the number of ferns changes with distance from the edge of a woodland, out into an open field. She also measures the light intensity at each point.
Name one abiotic factor, other than light intensity, that could affect where ferns grow. Name the equipment she could use to measure it.
questions.ms: Factor (1) with matching equipment (1): soil moisture + moisture meter; temperature + thermometer; soil pH + pH meter / indicator.

questions.q:
Her results are shown in the table.
Distance from woodland edge (m)0510152025
Light intensity (lux)8002 5006 00012 00018 00020 000
Mean number of ferns per quadrat14117311
Which type of graph should she use to show the relationship between light intensity and the number of ferns?
questions.ms: scatter graph (1).

questions.q: Describe the relationship between light intensity and the number of ferns.
questions.ms: As light intensity increases, the number of ferns decreases / negative correlation (1).

questions.q:
The student concludes: "Light intensity is the only factor that affects where ferns grow."
Evaluate her conclusion. Suggest how she could improve her investigation to make her conclusion more valid.
questions.ms: Level-marked. Level 3 (5–6): detailed and coherent, points linked in a logical sequence, correct terms. Level 2 (3–4): several relevant points with some linking. Level 1 (1–2): simple, separate statements. 0: nothing relevant. Evaluation: strong negative correlation; correlation does not prove causation; other abiotic factors change too (moisture, temperature, wind); biotic factors (competition from grasses); only one transect so may not be representative. Improvements: several transects; measure other factors at each quadrat; more quadrats / smaller intervals; conclusion: light likely important but not shown to be the only factor. No improvements caps at Level 2.

questions.q:
Balance these equations:
CH₄ + ___ O₂ → CO₂ + ___ H₂O
___ Na + Cl₂ → ___ NaCl
questions.hint: Type the four missing numbers in order, first equation then second, like 1,2,3,4
questions.ms: CH₄ + 2O₂ → CO₂ + 2H₂O (1); 2Na + Cl₂ → 2NaCl (1).

questions.q:
When calcium carbonate is heated, it breaks down: CaCO₃ → CaO + CO₂
Calculate the relative formula mass (Mr) of calcium carbonate, CaCO₃.
The M<sub>r</sub> of calcium oxide, CaO, is 56. Calculate the maximum mass of calcium oxide that can be made from 25 g of calcium carbonate. (g)
questions.ms: 14 g. 100 g CaCO₃ gives 56 g CaO (1); 25 ÷ 100 = 0.25 (1); 0.25 × 56 = 14 g (1). Correct answer alone scores 3.

questions.q: A student heats 25 g of calcium carbonate and makes 11.2 g of calcium oxide. Calculate the percentage yield. (%)
Mass is conserved in chemical reactions. Explain why the mass of the solid decreases when calcium carbonate is heated in an open tube.
questions.ms: Carbon dioxide gas is produced (1); it escapes into the air, so it is not weighed (1).

questions.q:
Reactivity series (most reactive first): potassium, sodium, calcium, magnesium, aluminium, (carbon), zinc, iron, lead, copper, gold.
Which metal is found in the Earth's crust as the uncombined element?
questions.ms: gold (1).

questions.q: Copper can be extracted by heating copper oxide with carbon. Write a word equation for this reaction.
questions.ms: copper oxide + carbon → copper + carbon dioxide (1).

questions.q: Identify the substance that is reduced and the substance that is oxidised in this reaction. Explain your answer in terms of oxygen.
questions.ms: Copper oxide is reduced because it loses oxygen (1); carbon is oxidised because it gains oxygen (1).

questions.q: Explain how the method used to extract a metal from its ore depends on the metal's position in the reactivity series. Use examples from the reactivity series in your answer.
questions.ms: Level-marked. Level 3 (5–6): detailed and coherent, points linked in a logical sequence, correct terms. Level 2 (3–4): several relevant points with some linking. Level 1 (1–2): simple, separate statements. 0: nothing relevant. Indicative: unreactive metals like gold found pure, separated physically; metals less reactive than carbon (zinc, iron, lead, copper) extracted by heating the oxide with carbon; carbon more reactive so removes oxygen, oxide reduced; e.g. iron oxide + carbon → iron + carbon dioxide; metals more reactive than carbon (potassium to aluminium) can't be reduced by carbon; extracted by electrolysis of the molten compound, e.g. aluminium from aluminium oxide; electrolysis is expensive (electricity). Level 3 covers all three methods linked to reactivity, with examples.

questions.q: Which of these is a behavioural adaptation?
options: a polar bear has thick fur
questions.ms: swallows migrate in winter (1).

questions.q: Compare continuous and discontinuous variation. Give one example of each in humans.
questions.ms: Continuous can take any value in a range (1), whereas discontinuous falls into distinct groups (1). Continuous example: height / mass / hand span (1). Discontinuous example: blood group / tongue rolling / natural eye colour (1).

questions.q: Strawberry plants can reproduce asexually by growing runners. Give one advantage and one disadvantage of asexual reproduction for the strawberry plant.
questions.ms: Advantage: quick / one parent / no pollination needed (1). Disadvantage: no variation, so all could be killed by the same disease or environmental change (1).

questions.q: The catalyst inside a catalytic converter is made of platinum, arranged in a honeycomb structure. Explain why a honeycomb structure is used.
questions.ms: Large surface area (1), so more gas molecules touch the catalyst and the reaction is faster / less platinum needed (1).

questions.q: Which of these is a biotic factor?
questions.ms: a new disease (1).
